#1584. Stevenage vs Blackpool - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 26 Nov 2026 13:22, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 13:31

Looking to extend their unbeaten run to six matches in all competitions, Stevenage welcome managerless Blackpool to Broadhall Way on Saturday afternoon for the sides' final League One fixture of the month.

Boro followed up a 1-0 victory away to Notts County with a goalless draw against Sheffield Wednesday during the week, while the Seasiders claimed their first point under interim boss Steve Thompson thanks to a late Niall Ennis equaliser in an unlikely draw against Leicester City.

After suffering playoff heartbreak last season, where Stevenage finished sixth before losing to Stockport County in the semi-finals, the Hertfordshire-based club stuck with Alex Revell in the hope that the former striker could lead Boro one step further this time around.

However, after 14 League One matches, Stevenage sit 13th in the table with five wins, five draws and four defeats leaving them on 20 points, six adrift of the playoff places.

Despite that, they remain closer to the top six than the bottom four and have put together some encouraging results as they look to turn their slow start to the season around.

After beginning the month by securing their place in the next round of the FA Cup, Stevenage finished top of their EFL Trophy group thanks to a penalty shootout victory over Fulham Under-21s, before beating Notts County and drawing with recently relegated Sheffield Wednesday.

Their recent run of form has also seen them keep three clean sheets in four matches across all competitions in November, playing a major role in helping them maintain the best defensive record in League One, with no side having conceded fewer than their 13 goals.

Saturday will mark their 15th league outing of the campaign, a fixture that they marked with a 1-0 victory over Peterborough United just over a year ago to move top of the table, highlighting the stark contrast with their performances at the same stage last season.

As for Blackpool, they look set to play their third match under interim manager Thompson, who took charge at Bloomfield Road following the departure of Ian Evatt, who was relieved of his duties after a 57-game spell with the Seasiders.

Evatt left the Lancashire-based club following a 1-0 defeat to AFC Wimbledon, a result that left Blackpool 20th and level on points with teams in the relegation zone.

Thompson, who has previously had three other spells as Blackpool's caretaker manager, oversaw a 2-1 defeat to fellow strugglers Wigan Athletic before guiding his side to a 1-1 draw with recently relegated Leicester City.

The stalemate with the Foxes came courtesy of an 84th-minute equaliser from Ennis in a match where the Seasiders had just 22.9% possession and faced 30 shots, but the unlikely point was enough to keep them outside the relegation zone.

Thompson is expected to remain in charge for this weekend's fixture, with Blackpool yet to appoint a permanent successor to Evatt, while Matt Bloomfield and Richie Wellens have both been linked with the vacancy.

Should Blackpool secure what would be just their fourth league win of the season this weekend, they could head into December with a three-point cushion above the drop zone, giving their next permanent manager an opportunity to take charge of a side unbeaten in two matches, although they face a Stevenage team that defeated them both home and away last season.

After drawing at home to Sheffield Wednesday in midweek, Revell will be keen to keep his side unchanged and has the luxury of doing so after his squad came through the match without any fresh injury concerns.

Tommy Setford has played a key role in Stevenage's impressive defensive record, and the 20-year-old goalkeeper is expected to retain his place as he bids to register his fifth clean sheet of the season.

Revell will, however, remain without Jasper Pattenden, Dan Kemp and Jordan Roberts, who are all still sidelined through injury.

For what is likely to be Thompson's third and final match in charge of Blackpool, the former midfielder will once again be without several first-team players.

A sickness bug kept Bailey Peacock-Farrell, Josh Bowler and Finley Munroe out of recent matches, but all three returned for the clash with the Foxes and are expected to feature again this weekend.

Dale Taylor, defenders Josh Earl, Fraser Horsfall and Michael Ihiekwe, as well as captain George Honeyman, are all likely to remain unavailable for the trip to Hertfordshire.

Having scored his second goal of the season after coming off the bench last time out, Ennis is likely to be rewarded with a starting place and could replace either Dion Charles or Jerry Yates.

Setford; Vancooten, Casey, Piergianni, Earley; Phillips, Thompson; Sanderson, Broggio, Patterson; Magennis

Peacock-Farrell; Lyons, Casey, Ashworth, Munroe; Niskanen, Brown, Morgan, Hamilton; Ennis, Charles

With one of the best defensive side's in the English Football League meeting a team who have struggled to score on a regular basis, we see this one going only one way.

We expect the Seasiders' struggles to continue with Boro making it four unbeaten in the league and closing out November with a sixth win of the season.

#1581. Liverpool transfer news: Who is Sidy Barhama Ndiaye, the 16-year-old Senegalese phenomenon expected in 2028?

By Axel Clody | 26 Nov 2026 13:28

Liverpool may have found their next great Senegalese talent. The Premier League club have reportedly reached a verbal agreement to sign Sidy Barhama Ndiaye, a 16-year-old winger who currently plays for Diambars.

However, Liverpool fans will have to be patient, as the young Senegalese cannot move to England until January 2028.

The news was revealed by Fabrizio Romano, who confirmed that a verbal agreement exists between the two parties.

Having already been given a trial by Liverpool in the summer of 2025, Ndiaye reportedly convinced the club's scouts, who have now secured an option on his arrival. Born on 31 December 2009, he will turn 18 at the end of 2027, which is a requirement for a move to England.

??? Liverpool have verbally agreed deal to sign 16 year old winger Sidy Barhama Ndiaye, here we go! Senegalese talent to join in January 2028, when he turns 18. Ndiaye was already at Liverpool on trial in 2025 and ready to become #LFC player for future. https://t.co/DrBIfNkPJR

A product of Diambars, one of the most renowned academies in Senegal, Sidy Barhama Ndiaye plays mainly on the right but can also operate on the left. He first caught the eye at the 2025 Under-17 Africa Cup of Nations, played when he was only 15, before continuing to progress with Senegal's youth teams.

His main qualities are his pace, his explosiveness and his ability to beat an opponent one on one. Very direct when receiving the ball, he likes to provoke, accelerate and create openings. He also has a degree of efficiency in the final ball, as he again demonstrated at the Under-17 World Cup.

During Senegal's 9-0 thrashing of Cuba, the young winger scored one goal and provided two assists. The performance helped to boost his reputation among European observers and scouts.

The comparison with Sadio Mane comes naturally around the young Senegalese.

Besides his origins, Ndiaye shares with his illustrious elder an attacking profile built on pace, penetration and the ability to make a difference on the wings. And if Liverpool, who benefited from Mane's talent for six seasons, complete the deal, that comparison will be unavoidable.

However, there is still a long way to go before he can be expected to play at Anfield. Between now and January 2028, Ndiaye will have to continue to progress at Diambars and confirm the promise shown with Senegal's youth teams.

Liverpool, for their part, have already taken a position on a player they want to integrate into their long-term project.

#1580. THE END GAME? Writing is on the wall for McCann after revitalised Dons ran riot at Rugby Park

Published: 18:00 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 18:11 EST, 22 November 2026

Let’s face it, Neil McCann was never the most popular of appointments with Kilmarnock fans, but not even his harshest critics could deny that he did a fine job in keeping the club in Scotland’s top flight last season.

Unfortunately for him, it looks increasingly likely that he isn’t going to get the chance to repeat the trick this time around.

The writing already appears to be on the wall for the 52-year-old. A question of when, rather than if, he is given his jotters.

By all accounts, he hasn’t lost the dressing room. Which is just as well, because he has well and truly lost the punters, whose collective mood shifted from angry to apathetic over the course of 90-odd thoroughly entertaining minutes at Rugby Park on Saturday.

McCann knows this himself. It is not as if he is operating with the blinkers on.

It's a tough watch for Neil McCann as his Kilmarnock team go down 4-2 to Aberdeen

His assessment of his team’s performances week-to-week tends to be pretty honest, as it was again this weekend.

The problem is, as he put it, that he is coming across ‘like a broken record’.

His team are hopeless at the back and toothless up top, with some encouraging stuff in between. If the supporters are sick of hearing it, imagine how scunnered McCann must feel saying it. He certainly looks it.

If they continue to defend like this, relegation is a nailed-on certainty.

They shipped four here — and it could have very easily been a few more — to take their tally to 33 conceded for the season in just 14 games. It’s laughable, there’s no other way to dress it up.

Aberdeen’s Kevin Nisbet scored twice in four first-half minutes, capitalising on a woeful clearance from keeper Nico Mantl to put the Dons ahead, before curling a free-kick straight through the weakest wall you’ve ever seen in your life to double the visitors’ advantage.

New Dons boss Mario Frick can't hide his delight after victory in first game in charge

The third goal — shortly after Greg Kiltie had given McCann’s men a lifeline — was the worst of the lot. Former Rugby Park skipper Brad Lyons ghosted in behind the completely unaware Michael Schjonning-Larsen to head the ball home after Cathal McCarthy failed to stop Nesta Guinness-Walker’s cross from the left touchline.

Shocking stuff all round, and exactly the type of goal which has killed Killie all season — and will continue to do so until something drastic changes.

Let’s not forget, the recent international break afforded McCann and his staff a fortnight to work on things on the training pitch ahead of what is going to be a gruelling winter schedule.

While the Killie manager will ultimately be the one to pay the price, his players need to have a right good look at themselves too. There was simply no sign of anyone in that backline taking any sort of responsibility.

Kilmarnock’s next three games are against St Mirren, Hibernian and Motherwell — the three sides currently directly above them in the table.

An absolute minimum of four points from that run is required, otherwise this is going to get rather ugly. In truth, defeat in Paisley this weekend may well be the final nail in McCann’s coffin.

On the other hand, things are finally starting to look up for the Dons.

New manager Mario Frick has promised to bring heavy metal football to these shores, and if Saturday is anything to go by, the ex-Liechtenstein international is a man of his word.

McCann's job looks to be on the line after bottom club Killie succumbed to another defeat

His team were a joy to watch going forward here, particularly in the first half.

It was a million miles away from the kind of turgid football offered up under his predecessor as Dons manager, Stephen Robinson.

Speed, intensity, aggression, quality. The performance was full of it.

You could count the number of times the Dons faffed about with the ball on one hand. Every time there was an opportunity to get forward, they took it.

Ante Palaversa, making his first appearance of the campaign, was at the heart of it.

For whatever reason, Robinson never fancied the Croatian, a stance which perplexed the Pittodrie faithful. Indeed, the 26-year-old — once on the books of Manchester City — was deemed surplus to requirements over the summer.

The Dons will be delighted there were no takers.

He was outstanding here as he commanded that space between midfield and defence without breaking sweat. Nobody in Killie colours could get near him.

Both Nicky Devlin and Guinness-Walker bombed up their respective wings all day, while some of the link-up play between Nisbet — who should have had a hat-trick before Findlay Marshall wrapped things up late on — and Hicham Mahou was delightful.

Defensively, they were all over the shop at times, and no doubt they will be punished heavily at Ibrox on Tuesday night if they are as open as this.

But this was a display to simply be enjoyed rather than picked apart. It makes a change.

Liverpool are finally starting to find their feet under Andoni Iraola.

The Reds record-breaking additions Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz have found form under the Spaniard, and Rio Ngumoha has continued his astronomical trajectory.

As is usually the case, Liverpool's upturn in form has led to interest in many of their stars from across Europe.

For several stars it feels like their time in Merseyside is coming to a natural end, but for others a move away would come as a surprise to the Anfield faithful.

Julian ward won't be looking to let any of Liverpool's best players go mid-season, but that hasn't stopped one European giant from trying to pry a duo away.

Bayern Munich eyeing Liverpool double swoopBayern Munich have some of the best attacking talent in the world. Hary Kane has just won the Ballon d'Or, Michael Olise is one of the most sought-after players in the world and Luis Diaz has continued his brilliance since moving on from Merseyside. The German giants have concerns over the long-term futures of Olise and Jamal Musiala however, and as a result are targeting a double swoop for Florian Wirtz and Rio Ngumoha.

Bayern Munich have some of the best attacking talent in the world.

Hary Kane has just won the Ballon d'Or, Michael Olise is one of the most sought-after players in the world and Luis Diaz has continued his brilliance since moving on from Merseyside.

The German giants have concerns over the long-term futures of Olise and Jamal Musiala however, and as a result are targeting a double swoop for Florian Wirtz and Rio Ngumoha.

That's according to an article from TEAMtalk, which states the German side are eying the Liverpool pair as well as Manchester City's Jeremy Doku as contingency planning begins for Olise and Musiala's potential exits.

The club's interest in both of the Liverpool pair extends back some way, with Bayern being heavily linked with both players in the past, but news of a potential move for both is new.

Any offer would have to be astronomical for Liverpool to consider the sale of either star, so the notion that they may sell both players to the same club is almost unthinkable.

There may have been a willingness to listen to offers for Wirtz in the past, but the German has turned a corner in the last six weeks and has a clear place in Iraola's plans.

Bayern may well try and sign the Liverpool duo, but it will likely be a firm no from Ward and the Anfield hierarchy.

#1577. Frosinone vs Parma - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 26 Nov 2026 13:47

Both beaten 5-1 last weekend, Frosinone and Parma will aim to bounce back when they clash at Stadio Benito Stirpe on Saturday.

Despite suffering consecutive defeats for the first time this term, the hosts are still 12 points above their visitors in the Serie A standings.

Frosinone made an unexpectedly strong start to their latest comeback campaign, scoring freely while winning six of their first 11 fixtures after returning to Serie A.

However, Massimiliano Alvini's attack-minded side then suffered a rare setback, going down 1-0 to Cagliari, before they were well beaten just after the international break.

Two goals down within 20 minutes, the Canarini continued to fly forward, but they never really recovered and ultimately lost 5-1 to AC Milan at San Siro.

In fact, Frosinone have only claimed two points on the road since beating Fiorentina at the end of August, so their form at Stadio Stirpe has kept them tucked inside the top half.

After narrowly losing their first home fixture against Juventus, they have since won all of the next five, so confidence should still be high when lowly Parma come to town.

While their promoted hosts sit seventh in Serie A, Parma are hovering above the relegation zone with just eight points on the board.

Like Frosinone, they were thumped 5-1 last week, as Roma stormed to victory at Stadio Tardini, with Capocannoniere leader Donyell Malen helping himself to four goals.

That was the Gialloblu's eighth defeat from their first 12 league games, and the recent hiring of their second-highest Serie A scorer has hardly had an impact.

Alberto Gilardino has only celebrated one win since succeeding Carlos Cuesta, who kept the Emilian club afloat last term, but that lone success did come on the road.

Following a run of six straight away defeats, Parma recently beat Atalanta 3-0 in Bergamo, so they will aim to claim more points when they head south on Saturday.

Now trailing Malen in the race to be crowned Italy's top scorer, Frosinone striker Antonio Raimondo is still sidelined by injury - and his deputy is also unavailable.

Daniel Birligea bagged a brace against Lecce before scoring for Romania in their recent Nations League camp, but he strained a hamstring in Milan and has been ruled out for the next few weeks.

So, it remains to be seen whether Alvini selects support forwards Fares Ghedjemis, Romano Schmid and Giorgi Kvernadze - each of whom have provided four Serie A assists - or Slovak centre-forward Tomas Bobcek to lead the hosts' attack.

On the absence front, Florian Grillitsch has yet to recover from a thigh problem, but left-back Gabriele Bracaglia can return after serving a one-match ban.

While Parma will welcome back Abdoulaye Ndiaye from suspension, Argentine striker David Romero is still ruled out by a serious shoulder injury; defensive duo Diego Carlos (thigh) and Dominik Drobnic (foot) are also doubts.

In Romero's absence, Simone Lontani could partner El Bilal Toure, but Nesta Elphege is also a contender after scoring the Gialloblu's lone goal against Roma.

Palmisani; Oyono, Monterisi, Calvani, Bracaglia; Masini, Calo; Ghedjemis, Schmid, Kvernadze; Bobcek

Daffara; Delprato, Troilo, Ndiaye; Britschgi, Fabbian, Sierro, Keita, Valeri; Elphege, Toure

Frosinone can arrest their decline with another home win, as Parma are in grim form and could face a long fight to avoid the drop.

Notably, the Canarini tend to start fast - scoring a league-high 11 goals inside the first 30 minutes - while their visitors have yet to score before the half-hour mark.

#1576. Opinion: Liverpool prepare for major tactical shift as new long-term target emerges

Andoni Iraola has now managed to get Liverpool to fourth in the Premier League table.

Obviously, this is still miles away from where they need to be but, the fact that only seven points separate them and first-placed Arsenal is excellent news.

Right now, it's unclear where Liverpool are going to finish in England's top flight but, if they keep performing to the standard they showed on Sunday against Manchester United, they'll be storming their way up the table.

But, for them to do this, improvements need to be made to their squad as, all of their other title rivals will be adding extra firepower to their ranks.

So, the fact that the January transfer window is now just over a month away is rather exciting.

Especially with all the players that they've just been linked with.

Liverpool see Gustavo Varela as a 'long-term target'

Liverpool have several problem areas among their ranks that need addressing.

Obviously, since they're one of the biggest clubs in the world, they won't have any problem finding players who want to join.

However, the prices that Premier League clubs have to pay instantly have extra money added on top of them.

That's why only a certain number of deals can be struck by Liverpool in each window.

Moves for the future are also laid out with a new update from Football Insider sharing that the Reds' recent links with Monza striker Gustavo Varela are for the 'long-term' rather than the short-term.

"Liverpool will not prioritise a move to sign Monza striker Gustavo Varela in January, sources have told Football Insider," they wrote.

"The 21-year-old has emerged as a target for the Reds, having struck 11 goals from his opening 11 games in Serie A so far this term.

"The Reds are "keeping tabs" on the Portuguese youngster, with several top Italian clubs also having their "eyes fixed on him" at the moment.

"However, sources say that Varela is viewed as more of a long-term option at Anfield, and the club are not likely to make a move for him this winter.

"Monza are relaxed over their frontman's future for now, but they know that further interest from top clubs is inevitable if he continues to perform."

Liverpool's interest in Gustavo Varela could mean that they're changing to a two striker formation

Liverpool only have two fit strikers among their ranks at the moment.

Alexander Isak is one of them and, since he was the Reds' record signing, he's obviously going to be Iraola's striker.

Lewis Koumas is the other and, even though his manager likes him, the fact that Hugo Ekitike is edging closer to a return will certainly worry him.

Before he got injured last term, Ekitike was easily Liverpool's best player and, they probably wouldn't have qualified for the Champions League if it wasn't for him.

So, the fact that Varela is now emerging as a potential option for the Reds on their shortlist certainly raises a few questions.

The easiest explanation for this move would be that, eventually, Iraola wants to move to a two striker formation while having Varela and Koumas as his back-up options.

Obviously, there are now guarantees that this will play out like that but, if that is the case, a major tactical change could be on its way to Anfield in the next couple of years.

#1575. Xabi Alonso hits out at ‘soft’ Chelsea players

Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.

Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.

Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.

The club’s dreadful clean-sheet record pre-dates him and is the first time in 65 years Chelsea have gone 20 league games without keeping the opposition out.

Hull’s first goal from Mohamed Belloumi came after the ball had bounced over Jorrel Hato and Alonso said: “We need to be aware that from any situation, any team in the Premier League can hurt you. Today it was from a long ball, two bounces, the way it happened. You need to be very aware, very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished and we have been punished that way.”

Chelsea have shared 30 goals with their opponents in the club’s six games in all competitions so far this season.

“Yeah, it’s all maybe entertaining, but I hope that one day you say it was a boring game and we win and we don’t give these entertaining moments,” he said.

“But, for sure, it kind of repeats some patterns that we are making. It will take time to... or it will take moments to fix them when we get the lead and you still need to be competing and not give the chance so easily for them to come back, especially in the first goal, we can do much better.

“It was too soft to give them this hope because until then we were controlling, we were creating chances. But that momentum that we had changed the mood and the score of the game, and it’s something that we need to be talking [about], we address and we will get better. But it’s having an impact on our performances at the moment.”

Asked if his players have a real desire to defend and keep clean sheets, Alonso said: “We can do better, we can do better for sure. We need to know that even when we have the lead, a very important part of the game is to hold together, to keep the distance, to go intense in the situations to defend. I’m sure that we can do better.

“Overall, I think that we are attacking better than defending in every part. We know that it’s a big topic and a big theme for us. For sure, it’s just four games. But the dynamic in terms of conceding, I don’t like it and we need to do much better. Open play, set-pieces, long balls, this toughness, this competitive sense, we can do better.”

Needing three goals or more to win games is not sustainable, as Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is finding out.

This is not a problem of Alonso’s making, given Chelsea have now gone 20 Premier League games without a clean sheet. But he is certainly not improving the issue yet.

Chelsea beat Fulham with three goals and Brighton with four but left themselves far too much to do against Arsenal and were taken advantage of by Hull City, who will be slightly disappointed they did not leave Stamford Bridge with all three points.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez has now conceded seven goals in three games since joining from Aston Villa, while central defender Maxence Lacroix, who joined for £52m from Crystal Palace in the summer, was relegated to the substitutes’ bench.

Martínez was at fault for Mohamed Belloumi’s second goal, but the Argentine did make a crucial save at his back post to stop substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho grabbing a winner that Chelsea could have had no complaints about.

Hull finished the game with more shots on goal than their hosts and a higher expected-goals rate. Chelsea are far too open and in some ways far too entertaining.

Defensive midfielder Moisés Caicedo cannot return from injury quickly enough, but this does not feel like a problem that will be solved by one man. Alonso needs to find a balance and instil a real desire in his team to defend.

Caicedo has that desire, but there are no defenders at the club who have shown that absolute desperation to keep the ball out of the net that Chelsea fans became so used to in the days of John Terry, Gary Cahill and César Azpilicueta.

None of this should diminish Hull’s performance. They were not only spirited and full of character but also showed quality and a threat. The joke is currently on those who laughed at their hopes of survival before a ball had been kicked.

It is now two wins and two draws for Sergej Jakirovic’s team and they are already a fifth of the way to 40 points. Jakirovic had promised his staff a week off in the international break if they reached eight points after five games. With that target already met, there may be a new reward if Hull can make it 11 points against Newcastle United next weekend.

“Before the season, I said to my staff that we will take seven, eight points in these first five and then I will give them seven days off,” Jakirovic said. “That was our target and now we are in a very good position, eight points.

“Especially today, it’s very, very difficult to play here, and now we will try to get even more. Of course, I’m a little bit worried about the international break because we have 13 national team players. But we will see who will come back and in what condition. So this is my concern right now.” Asked if his staff’s seven-day break will be extended if Hull can beat Newcastle, Jakirovic added: “I will tell them. But I know already.”

While his five-game target may need modifying, Jakirovic is not deviating from his goal for the season for Hull. “Our target is always to stay in the league and collect as many points as possible,” he said. “Forty points, 38 to 41, this is the average we need. Then it’s easier to play. You can play more relaxed, with more joy and happiness. So [get to] this as soon as possible, so that we are safe.”

Hull had not conceded a league goal before this and there had been predictions they might crumble when they finally let the ball into their net. They did so after just seven minutes but they kept their heads and came back stronger.

It was far too easy for Morgan Rogers to make a yard of space for himself to shoot after collecting the ball from João Pedro, and Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis may not have been happy to have been beaten at his near post.

Chelsea have now scored inside the first 10 minutes in all of their four league games, but Hull were in no mood to crumble and hit back with two goals in six minutes from Belloumi to take a half-time lead. Both Hull goals were shockers from Chelsea’s perspective. The first, in the 28th minute, came as a result of Jorrel Hato letting the ball bounce over him from a Ryan Giles cross and Belloumi finished brilliantly.

Belloumi’s second came after Martínez had flapped at a corner and Semi Ajayi had hit the bar with a header. The ball fell to Belloumi again and his shot was deflected into the net.

It was no surprise that Hato did not reappear for the second half, as he was replaced by Pep Chavarría at left-back. But Chelsea remained vulnerable and Martínez had to recover from spilling a Regan Slater shot to prevent Ollie McBurnie extending Hull’s advantage.

When Palmer and Pedro combined for Pedro to sweep the ball into the net and equalise with 24 minutes remaining, it seemed like it would be Chelsea who would provide the grandstand finish.

But it was Hull who got a second wind and Chelsea were indebted to Martínez for making a save to stop Cho securing all three points and sending the visiting fans home even happier.

I feel good. We have to be happy. It’s a huge result for us.

We had 2-1 at half-time and we had a 100 per cent chance with McBurnie but Martinez’s save was excellent. We have to control play better in the box because we can stop this [Chelsea goal]. We had an excellent chance for Cho – Martinez saved again. Player of the match.

We can be very happy. We took a point in a very demanding match.

Eight points against very difficult opponents. We have to continue like this.

There have been 12 Premier League games at Anfield in 2026, Liverpool have only won 4 of them to date. This was seventh draw and Fulham deserves their share of the spoils. This was very much a learning experience for Andoni Iraola.

Not a single home win in the Premier League, today.

Aston Villa 1 Nottingham Forest 2Bournemouth 2 Brentford 2Chelsea 2 Hull City 2Crystal Palace 2 Ipswich Town 3Liverpool 0 Fulham 0

What a result for Hull, who remain unbeaten and they have taken five points from fixtures against United, Villa and Chelsea.

That is the first really poor result of the Alonso era, points dropped.

What a thriller in SE25, both teams have been going for it in the closing stages, but Ipswich have surely score the winner through Zian Flemming.

Fulham were pointless before this game, but they have kept a clean sheet at Anfield with a disciplined display and they could well have score one or two. Underwhelming for Liverpool, who have not won just one of their first four games and their fixtures have not been the most taxing.

And as we predicted at the beginning of the game... Liverpool 0 Fulham 0. If this reporter ever gives you advice on a horse to back or a team to follow, make sure you take the opposite stance. Fulham deserve their reward and their fans are singing “We got a point!”

Villa are finishing the game with 10 men because Ian Maatsen pulled up after Emery had made his five substitutions, and Forest have punished them through Igor Jesus with just a few minutes of normal time to play.

Alexander Isak heads over the bar when he perhaps should have hit the target. Has time run out for Liverpool?

You might imagine Chelsea are battering down the door, but Mohamed-Ali Cho has just forced Emi Martinez into a save at the other end. Hull will remain unbeaten if they can hold out.

Strand Larsen has had his critics, but he has scored his first goal of the season to set up a grandstand finish with 15 minutes plus stoppage time to play at Selhurst Park.

Short corner, McGinn whipped in an inswinging cross that is glanced into the bottom corner by Alysson.

Liverpool continue to toil at Anfield, but no opening goal. Iraola has thrown on Frimpong, Mac Allister, Ngumoha and Gakpo in the second half. Fulham have had the chances to score at least one, and Josh King has just brought a save out of Alisson.

Hull are a little lucky they still have 11 men on the pitch. Already on a booking, my man Crooks bundled down Rogers. It could easily have been another yellow car but the referee let him off and now he’s been replaced by Iroegbunam.

Joao Pedro finds the smallest of gaps to be the goalkeeper and find the roof of the net with a brilliant, instinctive finish.

That had not really been coming for Chelsea. It all felt a bit easy for Palmer to get his low cross into the box and Pedro to sweep the ball in. The home fans have woken up again.

Martinez was lucky to get away with another slip up, there. He spilt Slater’s shot but reacted before McBurnie to stop the Hull striker scoring the rebound. Just a day after his nasty looking crash, Sorba Thomas is on for Hull.

This game is absolutely here for Fulham to win. Quietness has descended around Anfield, the hosts have no fluency in their play and Fulham are growing in confidence. Why wouldn’t they after getting to 65 minutes with a clean sheet?

Just like in the first half, four minutes after one of these teams taking the lead there has been an equaliser. Kevin Scahde is in a rich vein of form.

Bournemouth have have never beaten Brentford in the Premier League, but they might well be on their way to changing that record having trailed earlier in the game. Marcus Tavernier has just scored their second goal.

Matt Davidson Rider Crooks has just been booked for a very cynical foul on Rogers. It gave Chelsea a free-kick in a dangerous position Reece James had an effort tipped away. Chelsea have started the second half well

Within a minute of the restart, Villa lose the ball in midfield and Delap punishes them to the maximum. Cracking finish from just outside the box, and a much-needed goal by Delap. The Glasner curse striking for Emery again?

Liam Delap has just started paying back that £50m transfer fee with a fine goal.

Delap picked the ball up on the left and set himself up on the edge of the box before crashing a 25-yard shot past Zion Suzuki.

Unai Emery has made a couple of changes at half-time, taking off Nicolas Jackson who picked up a silly booking just before half-time.

Tammy Abraham is on in his place. George Hemmings is also off and replaced by Alysson.

Pep Chavarria on for Chelsea at half-time. He’s replaced Jorrel Hato, who had a bit of a stinker in the first half.

Andoni Iraola hasn’t hung about here. Milos Kerkez has come on immediately after half-time for Kostas Tsimikas and you can say with certainty that Liverpool will be shopping for a new left-back in due course.

So at half-time, Hull City are top of the Premier League and don’t their supporters know it? They were singing “we are top of the League” for the full two minutes of time added on for stoppages at the end of the first period. Alonso has some work to do at the break.

Forest did need a brilliant double save from Matz Sels to deny Victor Lindelof and have recovered to slow the match down.

Neco Williams wasted a decent chance for Forest from outside the penalty area shortly before the break.

Referee Andrew Madley has irritated both teams with a number of weird decisions - but that’s sadly par for the course with officials nowadays.

Villa 0 Forest 0Bournemouth 1 Brentford 1Chelsea 1 Hull City 2Palace 1 Ipswich 2Liverpool 0 Fulham 0

Palace in some trouble now, level with Ipswich and down to 10 men. Disasi was sent off in the 34th minute for a reckless challenge on Jack Clarke, caught him with studs on shin.

Things got worse for Palace just before half-time, with Leif Davis heading home at the back post to give Ipswich the league.

Apologies for the lack of updates, some technical gremlins at Telegraph Towers. A nip and tuck game as expected at at the Vitality: Kevin Schade gave Brentford the lead before Justin Kluivert equalised four minutes later.

One way to put it is that Kostas Tsimikas isn’t playing well. Another way to say it would be that his efforts are making Milos Kerkez look like Roberto Carlos. The Greek left-back is having a dreadful afternoon and Fulham are getting plenty of joy out of him. We suggested there was no chance of this game finishing goalless, and it’s anomalous that we have reached 40 minutes without score. Fulham, certainly, have a sense of adventure and have been into Liverpool’s 18-yard box plenty of times. Let’s see if the picture changes before the interval.

That’s now seven goals Emi Martinez has conceded in three games since joining from Villa to supposedly solve Chelsea’s goalkeeping crisis. Martinez won’t be pleased with Hull’s second goal, here. He was beaten to a corner by Ajayi. His header hit the bar and Belloumi’s shot was deflected past him. The Hull fans are in dreamland.

This is a turn up for the books. Chelsea undone by a long ball forward, and Hato lets the ball bounce over his head, and Belloumi finishes with aplomb.

That’s now 20 Premier League games Chelsea have gone without keeping a clean sheet. What an earth was Jorrel Hato doing, letting the ball bounce over him for Belloumi? Amateur stuff at the back from the home side. It was Hull’s first meaningful attack.

Emersonn has struggled in some games so far this season, but he has just planted a header into the corner from a Davis cross.

There is a VAR check for offside... but the goal stands.

5 - Morgan Rogers is the fifth different player to score or assist in each of Chelsea's first four games of a Premier League season, after Didier Drogba (2010-11), Cesc Fàbregas (2014-15), Diego Costa (2014-15 & 2016-17), and Eden Hazard (2018-19).Famous. pic.twitter.com/0cuThzH472

A sweet strike from one of Palace’s summer signings, recruited from Union Saint Gilloise, and that is his first Palace goal. The 22-year-old Israeli came through at Maccabi Haifa. Uphill task for Gary O’Neill and Ipswich.

Austin MacPhee, Chelsea’s flamboyant set-piece coach, just motioned for Xabi Alonso to sit down when the Blues manager momentarily got up from his seat when the home side were preparing to take a corner. It seems MacPhee wears the (correct length) trousers when it comes to set pieces.

An almighty let off for Alisson and Liverpool after pass from the goalkeeper played Gravenberch into trouble, but Jacquet cleared off the line to keep the game goalless. That was Fulham’s first foray forward.

A bright start in this game and there is no chance it will end goalless (famous last words). Andoni Iraola has made three changes from the team that beat Atletico Madrid on Wednesday and it’s a pattern of his early management that he is making the kind of decisions that supporters are nodding along in approval with. Liverpool should already be one up but Alexander Isak’s shot has just drifted across the face of goal but the signs are encouraging. It could be a long afternoon for Alvaro Arbeloa.

Wow. Unbelievable double save from Forest’s Matz Sels there to keep out Victor Lindelof.

The first was the most impressive, a reflex stop after a deflection.

Morgan Rogers is the first player to score against Hull City this season. Emi Martinez launched the ball forward after claiming a corner, and Rogers’ shot from the edge of the area crept under the goalkeeper Tzolakis. He will not want to watch that one again.

We’re past five minutes and it’s the longest Chelsea have gone without scoring in the league this season. Back on Matt Crooks – one of his middle names is Rider.

Although Rogers scored in the seventh minute...so the early goals continue for Chelsea. It will be difficult for Hull now.

Twelve seconds in and the chant “where were you in Istanbul” gets a very early airing from Villa’s home fans.

The early indications are that Reece James is playing in midfield with Malo Gusto at right-back in a conventional back four.

Xabi Alonso has made an encouraging start to life as Chelsea manager. But his trousers upset me. They are three inches too short and a bit baggy above the ankle.

We are under way in the five Premier League 3pm kick-offs. Goals and further updates from around the grounds as they happen.

Some early #analysis from Matt at the Bridge, about one of Hull’s midfielders.

Unai Emery has been very impressed with the academy graduate, who made his Champions League debut on Tuesday night.

There is also a big buzz around £51m signing Johan Manzambi, who is on the bench today after recovering from a knee injury.

Will we get another fast start from Chelsea today? They have scored inside the first five minutes in all three of their League games this season. Hull are yet to concede.

Hull are really tough to beat. They have played against some good opponents and they’ve kept them out - they haven’t conceded yet. It is going to be difficult because they are really organised but we are at home and it is on us to make the game about us.

We are very excited about our first European game coming up but we haven’t really spoken about it lately because we have just spoken about this game. This is a big game and we are looking for our first three points of the season. We have been close in every game so we hope to get it today.

Unai Emery is possibly the best coach in the Premier League but has found past encounters with Oliver Glasner very uncomfortable.

Since Glasner’s arrival in English football with Crystal Palace in February 2024, he has faced Emery’s Villa seven times and never lost.

With five victories and two draws, it is an impressive record albeit with a different set of players.

Aston Villa and Forest are two teams in transition, and meet for the first time since that two-legged Europa League semi-final last season.

Villa are building a new chapter after a summer of significant change, while Forest are implementing a totally different style of play under Oliver Glasner.

There have been signs of progress at both of the former European Cup winners. Villa secured an impressive victory over Club Brugge in the Champions League on Tuesday. Forest are improving under Glasner, with their best performance the 2-2 draw at Liverpool.

Returning to Villa Park will have some bitter memories for a number of the Forest players, after that 4-0 defeat in the second leg of the Europa League.

#1574. Tonali explains his ‘two stories’ with Milan after turning from fan into player

Sandro Tonali has once again revealed his love for AC Milan, and spoke of the emotion of playing for his boyhood team.

Tonali played for Milan from 2020 to 2023, making 130 appearances and scoring seven goals, winning the Scudetto in 2021-22. He moved to Newcastle for €64m in what was a painful exit, given that he was being talked about as a potential future captain.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

With the Magpies, the Lodi-born midfielder played 110 games, scoring 10 goals, before moving to Tottenham Hotspur in the last summer window for €108m. There, he has linked up with Roberto De Zerbi, someone who also has Milan in his heart.

There continues to be sporadic rumours about a return to the Rossoneri one day, but given his value it remains a pipe dream for now. Tonali was interviewed by Fútbol Emotion Italia and he recalled some significant moments that he had at Milan, with his comments relayed by Calciomercato.com.

“I have two stories with AC Milan. The first is up until I was 20, when I had never fully embraced the AC Milan world. The second is from 20 onwards for the following three years,” he began.

“I was a fan for a long time. Then when the matches allowed it, maybe there was a game at San Siro when in Serie B we almost always played on Saturdays, we often went to watch. It was something passed down in the family from my father, so I’ve always had it even since I was a child.

“Then past 20 years of age it changed, because as a player you can’t maintain the same relationship with the team that you have as a fan. I did that the first year too, but I felt it too much, so after that I experienced it differently.

“But maybe it was even more beautiful because you put the fan aside and you started to realise that I suddenly found myself there, with the team of my heart and in a stadium like San Siro.

“The first year wasn’t easy, I found myself struggling a bit. But it went well for me also from the point of view of playing without fans. It wasn’t nice, but for me personally as a player at that moment it was good because there was less pressure.

“But all in all it was bad because that year without fans it all seemed like friendlies, it didn’t feel like football. Milan means a lot to me.”

As has been the case after each of their three Championship defeats so far this season, Birmingham City bounced back from last weekend's Stoke City disappointment by claiming three points, this time at the expense of crisis-hit Burnley.

#1572. 'I reckon:' Liverpool verdict on 'physically dominant' sensation revealed

Liverpool have a lot of decisions to make before the end of the 2026-27 season.

Right now, they don't really look like they're going to be able to compete for the Premier League title or the Champions League.

Indeed, there are only seven points between them and first-placed Arsenal but, considering the Reds have already been beaten by Mikel Arteta's men once this season, that gap is going to be hard to break down.

Obviously, if they end up drawing or losing a couple of games like they did against Newcastle on Saturday, they could be in with a chance but, if it ends up being down to Liverpool, fans wouldn't really hold out much hope.

That is, especially since they were beaten 3-2 in the Champions League by Fenerbahce.

Changes are clearly needed at Anfield which is why the upcoming transfer windows are going to be massive for them.

Liverpool would have to slash Ronald Araujo's buy clause in half to sign him permanently

Nobody knows what Liverpool are going to do in the winter or summer transfer windows.

They have thrown their hat into many different rings with almost every position among their ranks covered by a new target or two.

Some players that the Reds have been linked with have been exciting for fans but others, not so much.

There are also some decisions to make about their current crop of players with Ronald Araujo's future being one of the most talked-about deals in the world.

Within their season-long loan deal, Liverpool have a €55 million option to buy the Uruguayan and, even though he's performed rather well, the Reds are still undecided about whether they want to activate that option to buy or not.

And, now, thanks to an update from David Lynch via Anfield Index, it's now clear what Liverpool's plans are.

"That figure [€55 million] is far too high for Liverpool to be interested," he said.

"You’re talking it would have to be, I reckon, about even half that much to even give a sniff of Liverpool being interested."

Liverpool need to make their decision on Ronald Araujo soon

Although there is still a long while until June comes around, a decision on Araujo needs to be made.

He's currently Liverpool's first-choice right-back and, without him among their ranks, even more problems would be coming the Reds' way.

Obviously, his prior experience of La Liga and the Champions League has massively helped him adjust to Premier League life but, since he's 27 years old and has a rather ropey injury history, it feels like a lot of money for Liverpool to commit to.

That is, especially when they don't know how good Conor Bradley is going to be upon his return from injury.

Everything is up in the air at then moment but, even if they don't want to, a decision is going to have to be made soon.

Otherwise, the Reds could end up missing out on the "physically dominant" defender or going for someone who's worse than the Uruguayan which would be far from ideal.

#1570. Mauricio Pochettino was immediately up against it in his first few days at this slow-motion car crash of a club - Man United's 4-0 loss at Liverpool showed how much he has to do: OLIVER HOLT

Published: 14:08 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 20:01 EST, 22 November 2026

A drone spied on his first training session, his star striker stayed up into the early hours obsessing over Grand Theft Auto the day he arrived, his best player has paused contract talks, his chief executive praised the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, and the club banned four supporters for three years for throwing a tennis ball on to the pitch.

That was before the football started. And the fates had decreed that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge as head coach of this misused, abused, diminished, fallen slow-motion car crash of a football club that was once Manchester United but which has lost all sense of its place in the modern football firmament was to be away to Liverpool at Anfield.

And then Pochettino picked a centre-half, Matthijs de Ligt, who had not started a Premier League game for more than a year. And De Ligt began the game by watching a long ball sail over his head as if it were a rare curiosity to be observed rather than to be dealt with and before you could blink, Leny Yoro had been sent off trying to clear up De Ligt’s mess.

So at least Pochettino got to see United set a new record. Yoro was sent off after seven minutes and 23 seconds and that has never been done more quickly by United in the league. So there was that. De Ligt went on, it is sad to report, to have such a dreadful game that it was tempting to watch it through your fingers. Not the best selection decision by the new boss.

And in the stands, Omar Berrada, the strangely bullish United chief executive, looked colder and colder and more and more pale in the chill and, beside him, Jason Wilcox, the director of football, slid deeper and deeper into his big coat until he nearly disappeared from view. Which, presumably, was what he was hoping to do.

Mauricio Pochettino was given a near-impossible task in his first game as manager of Manchester United

Leny Yoro (right) was sent off just minutes into their 4-0 defeat by rivals Liverpool at Anfield

The Reds dominated from then on, with teenage winger Rio Ngumoha one of the Reds' stars

And in the row behind them, Sir Alex Ferguson gazed down on what remained of the great club he had built. James Nesbitt, the esteemed actor who is Ferguson’s friend, sat next to him in the directors’ box. One of Nesbitt’s best performances was in The Missing. The United defence were starring in the remake.

And the Liverpool fans loved it. ‘You’re going down with the City,’ they sang at the United fans. ‘You’re getting sacked in the morning,’ they sang at Pochettino, as he stood, arms tightly folded on the touchline. When it got to 4-0, the Kop broke out another ditty. ‘Poch is at the wheel,’ they sang over and over again.

So, welcome to Manchester, Mauricio. Welcome to the sight of United consolidating their position one off the bottom of the Premier League. If they keep this going for another week, they will be in the bottom three of the top flight in December for the first time in more than 50 years. If Pochettino did not know it before, he knows it now: there is an awful lot of saving to be done on the red side of Manchester.

This is a relegation fight that United are in. Don’t kid yourself that it’s not. The last time they dropped out of the top flight in 1973-74, they won three games in their first 11 matches. This season, they have won just once in the first 11 and that was at home to Ipswich Town on August 30th. A lot of the teams around them have got something about them, too. They certainly have more spirit than this rabble.

In that context, it was not the best omen that this was the worst result in a United manager’s first game for more than 100 years. If Pochettino thought getting the USA to win the World Cup was a big ask, rebuilding United is up there with it. This is a club mired in dysfunction on and off the pitch. It is a Herculean task to rescue them and we are about to find out whether Pochettino has it in him.

It was strange seeing a new United manager anointed at Anfield as the crowd sang You’ll Never Walk Alone and the Kop flew its flags and the faces of Shankly, Paisley, Dalglish, Klopp and the rest stared down from the banner of all the bosses here who have won league titles. Pochettino stood on the sideline and drank it all in, right until kick off.

It was his misfortune that this is also a Liverpool team beginning to click. Florian Wirtz is beginning to express himself and that is a wonderful sight. Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak are becoming a formidable partnership. Rio Ngumoha scared Diogo Dalot rigid. Liverpool are rising again as United flounder.

It did not take long for Pochettino to get his first look at the uselessness that has afflicted United for most of this season. Only seven minutes had gone when Ronald Araujo drove a searching ball over the top of the United defence. De Ligt watched it go and abrogated responsibility for it, expecting Yoro to cover. Isak sprinted after it and by the time Yoro finally reacted, it was too late. Isak was on to it.

Pochettino opted to start Matthijs de Ligt (right) - but he struggled throughout the game

He knows the size of the task of saving United - and whether he can do it will determine his legacy as a manager

Liverpool, meanwhile, are starting to click - and Florian Wirtz is at the centre of that rise

Isak got ahead of Yoro and pushed the ball forwards. It was a heavy touch and would have run on to Lammens but Yoro compounded his error by bundling Isak down on the edge of the area. He was sent off by referee Sam Barrott. Only seven minutes and 23secs had elapsed. It was the quickest sending off in United’s Premier League history. It was not a controversy. It was just a show of defensive incompetence.

A free-kick in that kind of position might as well be a penalty when Dominik Szoboszlai is standing over it. He lashed it low and hard past the edge of the United wall. Bruno Fernandes shook a half-interested leg at it. It whistled past him and bulged the corner of the United net.

Liverpool (4-2-3-1): Alisson; Araujo (Gomez 85), Jacquet, van Dijk, Kerkez; Szoboszlai, Mac Allister (Nyoni 72); Barcola (Munoz 72), Wirtz, Ngumoha (Frimpong 78); Isak (Koumas 85)

Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Tsimikas, McConnell, Chiesa

Goals: Szoboszlai 10, Wirtz 13, Ngumoha 66, Munoz 82

Man United (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Dalot, Yoro, De Ligt, Martinez; Tielemans (Mount 65), Mainoo (Santos 87); Mbeumo (Maguire 22), Fernandes, Dorgu (Mazraoui 65); Cunha (Zirkzee 46)

Subs not used: Heaton, Heaven, Diallo, Lacey

Three minutes later, Liverpool were further ahead. Ngumoha embarrassed Dalot down the Liverpool left – not for the last time – and pulled a cross back for Wirtz. It was just behind the Germany playmaker but Wirtz has beautiful technique and somehow, he hooked it goalwards with his left foot and it crashed in off the underside of the bar.

United were in chaos. Pochettino looked stunned. He brought on Harry Maguire for Grand Theft Auto aficionado Bryan Mbeumo after 22 minutes. Maybe it was a bitter pill for Mbeumo. Maybe it will have just allowed him to spend more time with his PlayStation. Practice makes perfect, after all.

And so United spent the rest of the half repelling a siege of their goal. Fernandes summoned one shot on target but it dribbled apologetically through to Alisson from the edge of the area. Most of the time, though, it was like the Alamo at the United end. Maguire made one particularly heroic block from Isak.

Liverpool should have gone three-nil up just before the hour. Wirtz played a fine through ball to Barcola, who ran clear of the defence. Barcola had only Lammens to beat but instead of slotting the ball past him, he tried to dribble around him, got his feet mixed up and kicked the ball out of play.

There was frustration at Anfield. They wanted more than this. This was a chance to rub United’s noses in it, to inflict more misery on their hapless rivals. And yet, there was a sense they were letting them off the hook.

That feeling deepened when De Ligt made a dreadful mess of intercepting a lofted pass to Isak, missed his kick and fell over. Isak raced through but then blasted his shot hopelessly high and wide. Then Barcola turned De Ligt and hit another shot too high.

Liverpool could not keep missing all afternoon, though, and they finally got their third when Barcola skipped past Lisandro Martinez on the halfway line as if he wasn’t there and sprinted down the right. He squared the ball across the box to Ngumoha and Ngumoha slammed it unerringly past Lammens. Victor Munoz drilled home the fourth eight minutes from time and United’s humiliation was complete.

#1569. PSV Eindhoven vs. Go Ahead Eagles - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 26 Nov 2026 14:12

Looking to move on from their midweek Champions League collapse against Real Madrid, PSV Eindhoven return to the bread and butter of Eredivisie football on Saturday.

The defending champions welcome Go Ahead Eagles to the Philips Stadion in gameweek 14, seeking a response to their humbling experience in the Spanish capital as they chase a fourth consecutive top-flight victory.

An Ivan Perisic goal made things interesting at the Bernabeu in midweek, but a Jude Bellingham-inspired second-half performance saw Jose Mourinho's Los Blancos run riot and eventually claim a 5-1 victory over PSV.

That loss, the Dutch giants' third in five European matches, leaves them 30th in the 36-team league-phase standings and their top-eight prospects looking increasingly remote.

However, Peter Bosz's men remain in contention for the qualification playoffs, with 24th-placed Villarreal just two points ahead of the reigning Eredivisie champions.

The Farmers will undoubtedly welcome a return to home comforts on Saturday as they seek to regain winning momentum after their chastening experience in the Spanish capital.

League football has brought greater encouragement, particularly in recent weeks, with three consecutive victories following a run of one win in four matches between late September and late October.

Scoring at least four goals in each of their victories over Willem II (7-0), Cambuur (6-2) and NEC (4-1) suggests a return to their free-scoring best, boding well for this weekend's visit from Go Ahead Eagles.

The Deventer outfit travel to Eindhoven in indifferent form, with a 1-0 away victory over SBV Excelsior coming between defeats to Cambuur and Fortuna Sittard.

Particularly notable has been the attacking decline of Joseph Oosting's men, who have scored just once across their last three league matches after averaging 2.3 goals per game over the opening 10 gameweeks.

While that sample remains too small for firm conclusions, the Pride of the IJssel's dip cannot be dismissed ahead of their trip to the Philips Stadion, where Kowet claimed a stunning 2-1 KNVB Beker semi-final victory in February 2025 en route to lifting their first domestic cup.

Paul Simonis was in charge for that historic success as Go Ahead Eagles secured their first victory in Eindhoven for 57 years, and they now seek a first Eredivisie win at PSV since 1968.

That will be easier said than done, however, as their historical struggles and recent scoring decline leave them vulnerable against hosts still reeling from their Santiago Bernabeu beatdown.

Mauro Junior (groin), Sami Ouaissa (muscle), Adamo Nagalo, Alassane Plea and Jerdy Schouten (ACL) remain unavailable for PSV; however, Ricardo Pepi should feature in some capacity after remaining on the bench in Madrid.

No player has scored more Eredivisie goals than Sven Mijnans, with the versatile attacking midfielder registering nine strikes and three assists in the top flight.

Guus Til is likely to lead the attack despite Pepi's availability, while Ruben van Bommel offers a dual threat after contributing five goals and three assists.

Soren Tengstedt shares Mijnans's position atop the league's scoring charts, with no player outscoring the Kowet forward this season.

Stefan Ingi Sigurdarson (four goals, one assist) and Mathis Suray (three goals, four assists) also possess match-winning quality that Oosting will hope comes to the fore at the Philips Stadion.

Go Ahead Eagles remain without Pim Saathof (ACL), while Evert Linthorst and Dean James will be assessed closer to kick-off.

Kovar; Dest, Geertruida, Obispo, Kostic; Sano, Fernandez; Perisic, Mijnans, Van Bommel; Til

Go Ahead Eagles possible starting lineup:

Cillessen; Sampsted, Dirksen, Kramer, Baeten; Meulensteen, Rahmouni; Tengstedt, Edvardsen, Suray; Sigurdarson

PSV's collapse in Madrid exposed their limitations in Europe, but scoring 17 goals across their last three Eredivisie victories underlines the different challenge they present domestically.

Go Ahead Eagles have managed just one goal in their last three league matches, and the hosts have our backing to deliver a convincing response at the Philips Stadion.

#1568. GdS: Super in Serie A, struggling in Europe – the reasons behind the ‘two-faced’ Milan

AC Milan are having a positive start to the 2026-27 season in Serie A, but in the Europa League they have been poor. Why exactly is that the case?

Milan go into tonight’s game against Olympiacos needing a win in order to start putting things right in a competition in which they have so far lost three out of four. The top eight expectation has now vanished, with even a play-off spot in jeopardy.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

La Gazzetta dello Sport write that Amorim has been coaching two teams since the summer: one which is excellent in the league with some ups and downs, and another that is frankly terrible when the Europa League anthem players.

Milan score 2.33 goals per game in the league on average, compared to just 1 per game in Europe. All four of those goals in the UEL came in the win over RB Salzburg too: they have drawn a blank in the other three.

Looking a bit deeper, Milan have less possession in Europa League matches (53%, compared to 59% in the league) but shoot 12.5 times per game, more than in Serie A. In Europe they get into the box more often: 26 touches in the opponent’s box compared to 23.

So, why do they score so much less despite being more threatening? Simply put, they shoot worse: the Rossoneri have a very high conversion rate in Serie A (26.4%) which plummets to 10% in Europe. This means that in the UEL it takes 10 shots to score a goal, while in the league it only takes four.

It’s not all mathematics. Anyone who has watched Milan in Europe have noticed their difficulties. At Bournemouth, they were never in the game, against Ferencvaros they collapsed, against Benfica they deserved to lose against a fellow contender.

With just hours to go before the match against the best defence in the competition, another test awaits. However, Amorim must find a way to concede less too. In Europe, Milan concede 1.92 xG per game, while in the league it’s just 1.28.

This all leads to a discussion about line-ups, and Amorim has rotated a lot outside of league action. The right defender has always been Filippo Terracciano or Fikayo Tomori, never Mario Gila. Without the Spaniard, there’s a noticeable difference.

In midfield, Luka Modric has never started, and Adrien Rabiot started only against Salzburg and Ferencvaros. Up front, Diego Moreira started only against Bournemouth. Life, with or without those three, changes completely.

Amorim already knows he won’t have Modric against Olympiacos, but he can plan with Rabiot and Moreira, concocting a strong side despite the injury issues. He’ll ask for overtime tonight and on Monday in Cagliari, knowing his side will then have almost a week to rest.

#1567. Report: Andoni Iraola wants to bring versatile defensive sensation to Liverpool soon

Andoni Iraola's time as Liverpool's manager has delivered a bit of a mixed bag of performances so far.

The Spaniard was brought in to replace Arne Slot after the Dutchman led his title-defending team to a fifth-place finish.

Clearly, this performance was nowhere near good enough for a title-defending team and, change was definitely needed.

And, even though over £150 million worth of change came through the Anfield doors in the summer, more deals need to be struck so that Liverpool can start competing for silverware again.

So, even though the transfer window isn't open yet, there's no reason for the rumour mill to not continue turning.

Liverpool are eyeing a move for Mohamed Simakan

Alongside Liverpool's attack, their defence has been a big problem for them.

Whether its been a lack of form or just the sheer number of injuries they've suffered, things just haven't gone to plan for Liverpool's back line over the last couple of years.

That's why players such as Jeremy Jacquet, Ronald Araujo and Giovanni Leoni have all been brought in.

Right now, things are in a good place for the Reds' back four but, that could all change if they choose against signing Araujo permanently.

Nothing is set in stone yet but, the fact that Caught Offside have shared that Mohamed Simakan is now wanted by Liverpool proves that Iraola and Julian Ward are trying to line up some back-up options just in case things don't go to plan.

"Liverpool and Manchester United are both monitoring Mohamed Simakan as the Premier League rivals consider defensive reinforcements ahead of 2027," they wrote.

"The 26-year-old has remained an important figure for Al-Nassr since leaving RB Leipzig and offers the kind of profile that could appeal to both clubs.

"Comfortable at centre-back or right-back, Simakan combines pace and physical strength with experience playing in an aggressive defensive system.

For Liverpool and United, however, January may be too early for anything concrete. For Liverpool, Simakan’s versatility is particularly attractive.

"With long-term succession planning required in central defence, signing a player capable of operating centrally while also covering right-back would give the squad valuable flexibility."

Mohamed Simakan could become Liverpool's next Ronald Araujo

One of the best things about Araujo is that he can comfortably play as a right-back or a centre-back.

No matter which position he's used in, he's always been seen as one of the Reds' best players this term with fans demanding that his deal is made permanent.

Clearly, this hasn't happened yet and, since rumours have been emerging that the price of Araujo would have to be slashed in half for Liverpool to even consider doing that, the deal doesn't feel all that likely to come to fruition.

This isn't ideal news but, the fact that Simakan can be used as a centre-back or a right-back does mean that change is coming to Anfield.

He may have spent the last couple of years in the Saudi Pro League with Al-Nassr but, he's still only 26 years old so, even if he isn't up to scratch right away, he could develop and become better.

Nothing is set in stone yet but, since Iraola wants to bring him in, Simakan could end up being a name that Liverpool's fans get rather used to.

#1566. Real Madrid vs. Alaves: Head-to-head record and past meetings ahead of La Liga clash

By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 14:18, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 14:18

Real Madrid will be aiming to continue their excellent run of form when they welcome Alaves to Bernabeu on Saturday evening.

Los Blancos will enter the league fixture off the back of a thumping 5-1 victory over PSV Eindhoven in the Champions League.

Jose Mourinho's side have now won each of their last 10 matches in all competitions, including their last six fixtures in Spain's top flight.

Real Madrid beat Celta Vigo 2-1 in the league last time out, and they currently sit second in the La Liga table, three points behind the leaders Barcelona.

Alaves, meanwhile, have been one of the success stories in La Liga this season, picking up 16 points from 13 matches, which has left them in ninth spot in the table.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up the head-to-head record and looks at the previous meetings between the two teams ahead of their clash in the Spanish capital.

Real Madrid have tackled Alaves on 46 occasions throughout history, and unsurprisingly, the Madrid giants lead the overall head-to-head record with 38 wins to Alaves five, while there have only ever been three draws between the two teams.

Karim Benzema is the all-time leading goalscorer in this fixture, having scored nine times against Alaves during his time at Real Madrid.

Real Madrid are on 121 goals against Alaves, conceding just 34, and Los Blancos are on a nine-game winning run against the Basque side.

That said, Alaves do have a recent famous win over Real Madrid to their name, having recorded a 2-1 victory when the two teams locked horns at Bernabeu in November 2020, thanks to goals from Lucas Perez and Joselu.

Alaves have beaten Real Madrid only twice since 2000, though, while there has not been a draw between the two sides since October 2001.

Two of Alaves' five wins over Los Blancos have actually come at the Bernabeu, also triumphing 1-0 in the famous stadium back in 2000.

In La Liga, the teams have met on 40 occasions, with Real Madrid winning 34 times to Alaves' four, drawing twice in the process.

#1564. A tale of glory or misery in Greece: All the key stats ahead of Olympiacos vs. Milan

AC Milan and Olympiacos will face each other for a fifth time this evening, with the Greek side hosting the Rossoneri in Athens.

The first two meetings came in 1959-60 and the other two were in 2018-19. In the European Cup clashes in 1959, the Rossoneri prevailed 5-3 on aggregate after drawing 2-2 in Greece and then beating them 3-1 back at San Siro. Giancarlo Danova scored a hat-trick in the second leg.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The most recent encounters were eight years ago, as mentioned. Patrick Cutrone (2) and Gonzalo Higuain fired Gennaro Gattuso’s side to a 3-1 home group stage win. Yet, in Piraeus the Diavolo lost 3-1 on the final matchday to drop to third and crash out.

➤ Olympiakos have won one of their four major European matches against Milan (D1 L2), winning the most recent meeting 3-1 in December 2018 in the UEFA Europa League. The Rossoneri have never won an away major European match in Greece in six attempts (D4 L2), failing to score in three of those matches.

➤ Olympiakos have lost just one of their last 13 UEFA Europa League matches (W8 D4), keeping nine clean sheets. In the group stages, they’re unbeaten in 11 games (W7 D4), conceding just twice.

➤ Milan have lost three of their four UEFA Europa League games this season (W1), including their last two without scoring. They’ve never lost three major European games in a row without finding the net. Olympiakos’ Jota Silva has had the most shots in the UEFA Europa League this season (17) – however, he is yet to score with any of those attempts, only landing two of them on target.

➤ Milan have never won a competitive game against a Greek side in Greece, losing 2 and drawing 4. However, they have lifted the Champions League trophy twice in Athens (4-0 vs. Barcelona in 1994 and 2-1 vs. Liverpool in 2007).

➤ Hosts Olympiakos have won each of their two previous Europa League contests at Stadio Georgios Karaiskákis this season. Olympiakos will be out to prolong a six-match home unbeaten streak in all competitions.

➤ Milan have one win and one loss on their travels in the competition this season in two contests. In their last six matches in all competitions, Olympiakos have won four and drawn two. They scored 17 and conceded five over that stretch, scoring first in four of the six contests. They had five first-half goals, while their opponents netted two times in the first 45 minutes.

➤ Milan have won four and lost two in their last six. They scored 14 and conceded nine in that stretch, netting first in four of the six. Most of their goals (10) came in the first half, while their opponents netted three times before the break.

➤ Armando González has caught the eye for Olympiakos in Europa League play. He is their top scorer with two goals, one of which has been the tone-setting first of the match.

➤ Alphadjo Cisse has been the leading attacking threat for Milan, scoring on three occasions in the current Europa League campaign, including one match-opening goal. He is tied for third in the competition’s scoring charts in 2026-27.

➤ The visitors have found it challenging to score in Europa League play recently, as they are scoreless in their last 198 minutes in the competition. They haven’t been on the scoresheet since a Gonçalo Ramos goal in their league phase win against Salzburg.

➤ Milan may face difficulty scoring yet again, as Olympiakos are in the midst of a shutout streak and haven’t allowed a goal in their last three Europa League matches, dating to a Kajetan Szmyt finish in their league phase win against Jagiellonia Białystok.

#1563. Lionel Messi escapes red card after hurling ball into rival's face in brutal Inter Miami playoff loss

Published: 22:41 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 03:57 EST, 23 November 2026

Inter Miami star Lionel Messi was lucky not to have been sent off after hurling the ball in the face of his opponent during an embarrassing MLS Cup Playoff defeat.

In the Round of 16 contest against the Columbus Crew, Miami went down 1-0 early in the first half with a penalty converted by Gonzalo Tapia. The deficit was then compounded when Miami fullback Gonzalo Lujan was sent off with a second yellow card.

On the stroke of halftime, Messi nearly joined his teammate in the locker room with a moment of madness on a throw-in.

Tapia and Messi were both standing out of bounds as the Chilean striker prevented the World Cup winner from taking his throw right away.

Messi then used the ball to shove Tapia's face back. When the Columbus man tried jumping in the air to block the throw, Messi then threw the ball into Tapia's head.

Tapia crumbled to the ground as Messi raised his hands asking for a foul on the Crew star.

Lionel Messi takes a throw-in off Gonzalo Tapia's face pic.twitter.com/jX3tTuojHe

Lionel Messi nearly got sent off during his team's MLS Cup Playoff match against Columbus

A frustrated Messi launched the ball off the face of Crew striker Gonzalo Tapia as he prevented the Argentina star from taking a quick throw in. Both players received yellow cards.

Tapia got revenge by scoring a brace to lead the Crew to a 3-0 victory on Saturday evening

Referee Allen Chapman was not happy with either player's antics, showing yellow cards to both Tapia and Messi.

But ultimately, Columbus and Tapia would get the last laugh as they won 3-0 in the best-of-three Round of 16.

Midfielder Taha Habroune scored the second goal of the evening in the 52nd minute as Tapia secured a brace just six minutes later.

The result has Inter Miami on the brink of elimination from the playoffs after winning the title last season. Columbus dominated every facet of the game, thanks in part to owning 62 percent of possession.

Messi attempted two shots on the evening – counting for half of the saves from Crew keeper Patrick Schulte.

Inter Miami must win the next match in Ohio to stay in the playoffs. If the game finishes tied, the rules dictate the match will proceed directly to penalty kicks.

Out of his three prior seasons in the United States, Messi's 2025 MLS Cup victory was an outlier. Miami missed the playoffs in 2023 and were eliminated in the first round in 2024.
